topics.title: Raymond Burr’s Gay Husband and Maxwell House
topics.summary: A comedian recounts a story about Raymond Burr, fascinated by Maxwell House Coffee commercials after visiting his teenage father’s recording studio as a teenager; he exhibited stereotypical ‘queer’ behavior afterward – flitting around and acting strangely to the astonishment of everyone involved.

topics.title: Dice, Bells, and House Hunting
topics.summary: Richard Dice recounts his experience buying a mansion in Long Island after initially being wary of superstition surrounding the property. He describes encountering an attorney with African art collection and ultimately closing on the house despite initial concerns about potential bad luck.

topics.title: Superstitions, Celebrity Plugs & Rapid-Fire Questions
topics.summary: The broadcast features a chaotic discussion about superstitions like ladders and cracks. Jessica Hahn plugs her celebrity centerfold video featuring explicit scenes with a midget, while Max Casella promotes his role on ‘Doogie Howser’ and Howard attempts to steer the conversation towards romantic encounters involving celebrities, culminating in rapid-fire questions and product pitches.”} <start_of_image>\n 201432501100

topics.title: Richard Bell’s Nightly Calls and Florida Plans
topics.summary: Richard Bell discusses his nightly phone calls, a lost high school ring, and plans for comedy dates in Tampa, Fort Lauderdale, and Orlando. He details an unusual habit of watching Lady Chatterley's Lover to avoid his wife while discussing new curse words he intends to use on the road.

topics.title: Little Richard Award Controversy Revisited
topics.summary: During the radio show, Howard discusses Little Richard’s frustration with the Grammy organization after they initially offered only two tickets for his lifetime achievement award and then rescinded that offer. The situation highlights differing opinions about honoring musical icons and underscores a misunderstanding regarding acceptance protocols.
